Elaine Harper: Heads-up — Acme Analytics ETL exceeded per-key QPS cap again at 00:30. Their nightly batch spikes ~4-5x for ~12 minutes and then settles. Manual top-up worked but ops wants an auditable pattern.
Trent Cole: Which key? batch schedule? tagging @ops-sre makes sense.
Elaine Harper: key=acme-ingest (partner/internal). It's scheduled. We gave a console top-up yesterday. Ops asked for a formally recorded temporary lift flow so we don't rely on ad-hoc console clicks.
Yasmin Patel: I propose a "temporary lift" resource: {actor, key_id, delta_rps, ttl, reason, incident_link?}. Backend creates transient override record, enforcement layer checks memcache TTL. Console shows active lifts + audit entries.
Chris N.: Need strict RBAC. One-click for verified internal keys only. For external or partner-facing keys require approver. Also: no silent edits to overrides; only revoke allowed.
dev-platform-bot: Policy check: temp-lift request detected for key=acme-ingest by Elaine Harper — policy=temp-lift.v2 — auto-approve criteria: delta<=3x && ttl<=30m.
Trent Cole: API sketch:
```
POST /v1/keys/:key_id/lift
{
  "delta_rps": 150,
  "ttl": "15m",
  "reason": "nightly ETL",
  "requested_by": "elaine.harper"
}
```
Response: {lift_id, expires_at, audit_link}. Enforcement: check memcache for active lifts in fast path; fallback query DB if missing.
Elaine Harper: UX question: quick button near key row vs modal that forces TTL+reason? Ops wants low friction for on-call but also audit requirements.
Chris N.: Compromise: one-click for 5/15/30 preset TTLs but modal if custom TTL or delta > threshold. Include a required justification field and an optional incident link. For non-internal keys, route to approver flow. Send Slack/email notifications when created.
Yasmin Patel: Telemetry: attach lift_id and actor to request traces while lift active. Emit metric lifts.active.count and lifts.delta.ratio per-key. Add alert if lifted traffic >20% of key traffic for >10m. Also log who created it and the UI context.
ops-sre: I'll add runbook steps: how to revoke, validate traffic, and what to do if downstream systems degrade. Also include a check to auto-revoke if error rate spikes after lift.
Trent Cole: infra note: enforcement must be cheap — memcache with TTL and signed token for L1. Also add circuit-breaker to prevent a lift from cascading to worker queues. Revokes should be immediate (invalidate cache + emit revoke event).
Elaine Harper: Action items: 1) Trent: implement API + memcache prototype. 2) Yasmin: telemetry spec + alerts. 3) Chris: RBAC + approval policy doc. 4) Ops-sre: runbook + rollback procedures. I'll draft a short RFC + UI mock and add an example audit.
Chris N.: Also ensure override records are immutable after creation (status changes only: active->revoked->expired). No edits.
dev-platform-bot: RFC created: https://intranet.redwood.com/rfcs/124-temp-key-lift — assignees: Trent Cole, Yasmin Patel, Chris N., ops-sre — due EOW :calendar:
